title: What Lies Beneath the API — Benjamin Cowen, Modal
talk_summary: A Modal FDE argues that mature AI products eventually hit limits of frontier APIs (cost, latency, plateaued evals) and should consider fine-tuning open models, which is now cheap via serverless compute and open-source SFT/RL libraries. The talk is mostly a vendor pitch for Modal with no concrete engineering techniques beyond 'collect data and build evals now'.

takeaways.technique: Instrument evals as future training data
takeaways.what_they_do: Advises that if you already run an agent harness and evaluate outputs, you should persist pass/fail traces so they become a fine-tuning dataset later, rather than discarding them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're evaluating your products um and collecting that data on what's working and what's not, then you have training data to train your model

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune a small model for a narrow task
takeaways.what_they_do: Claims narrow business-logic tasks (e.g. support) can be beaten by a fine-tuned open model at a fraction of frontier API cost, served via vLLM on serverless GPUs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Intercom is beating their frontier API at 1/5 the cost

takeaways.what_they_do: Describes spinning up tens of thousands of short-lived sandboxes for embarrassingly parallel evaluation, killing unpromising runs immediately.
takeaways.evidence_quote: customer scaling up to 50,000, 100,000 sandboxes just to do RL
